introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2026. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory to all candidates) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) A particle moves from rest in a straight line from a fixed point $O$, and after $t$ seconds of its motion, the acceleration, $a$, of the particle is $a=(3-2t)\ \text{m s}^{-2}$. Find

(a) the velocity of the particle after 2 seconds. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Velocity is the integral of acceleration: $v=\displaystyle\int a\,dt=\int(3-2t)\,dt=3t-t^2+c.$

The particle starts from rest, so $v=0$ when $t=0$: $0=0-0+c$, hence $c=0$ and

$$v=3t-t^2.$$

At $t=2$: $v=3(2)-2^2=6-4=2$.

**The velocity after 2 seconds is $2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) the distance covered by the particle after 2 seconds. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The displacement from $O$ is the integral of the velocity, $v=3t-t^2$ (found in part (a)):

$$s=\int_0^2(3t-t^2)\,dt=\left[\frac{3t^2}{2}-\frac{t^3}{3}\right]_0^2=\left(6-\frac83\right)-0=\frac{10}{3}.$$

The particle never turns back during these $2$ seconds, because $v=t(3-t)>0$ for $0<t<3$, so the distance covered equals the displacement.

**The distance covered is $\dfrac{10}{3}\approx3.33$ m.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) In the diagram, a particle $A$ of mass 4 kg rests on a smooth horizontal surface. The particle $A$ is attached to an inelastic string which passes over a smooth fixed pulley at the edge of the table, to another particle $B$ of mass $m$ kg hanging freely. Given that the system is released from rest with the string taut, and particle $A$ moves along the plane with an acceleration $2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ [sic, an acceleration of $2\ \text{m s}^{-2}$]. Find

(a) the tension in the string. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The surface is smooth, so the **only horizontal force on $A$ is the tension $T$** in the string. Newton's second law for $A$ ($F=ma$):

$$T=4\times2=8.$$

**The tension in the string is $8$ N.**

(The string is inelastic and the pulley is smooth, so the tension is the same on both sides of the pulley and $A$ and $B$ have the same acceleration.)

For the hanging particle $B$ (mass $m$ kg, weight $mg=10m$ N, acceleration $2\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ downwards), the net downward force is $mg-T$:

$$10m-T=m\times2.$$

With $T=8$ (part (a)): $10m-8=2m$, so $8m=8$ and $m=1$.

Check with the whole system: driving force $mg=10m$ moves a total mass $(4+m)$: $10m=(4+m)\times2\Rightarrow8m=8$ ✓.

**$m=1$ kg.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(iii) A particle $A$ of mass $4$ kg moves on a straight line with velocity $3\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and collides with a particle $B$ of mass $3$ kg moving in the opposite direction with velocity $2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. After the collision particle $A$ moves with velocity $1\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Find

(a) the velocity of $B$ after the collision. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Take the original direction of motion of $A$ as **positive**. Before the collision: $A$ has velocity $+3$, $B$ has velocity $-2$ (opposite direction). After the collision: $A$ has velocity $+1$ and $B$ has velocity $v$.

**Conservation of momentum** (total momentum before = total momentum after):

$$4(3)+3(-2)=4(1)+3v\ \Rightarrow\ 12-6=4+3v\ \Rightarrow\ 3v=2\ \Rightarrow\ v=\frac23.$$

The positive sign means that $B$ now moves in the same direction as the original direction of $A$.

**The velocity of $B$ after the collision is $\dfrac23\approx0.67\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ (in the original direction of $A$).**

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii)(b) the loss in kinetic energy due to the collision. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Kinetic energy is $\tfrac12mv^2$ (speed squared, so the signs do not matter).

**Before:** $\tfrac12(4)(3)^2+\tfrac12(3)(2)^2=18+6=24$ J.

**After:** $\tfrac12(4)(1)^2+\tfrac12(3)\left(\tfrac23\right)^2=2+\tfrac12(3)\left(\tfrac49\right)=2+\tfrac23=\tfrac83$ J.

Loss of kinetic energy $=24-\dfrac83=\dfrac{72-8}{3}=\dfrac{64}{3}$.

**The loss in kinetic energy is $\dfrac{64}{3}\approx21.3$ J.**
